title: Review of c39's CIPS isotropy finding on fresh seeds 3 and 4 (ISO=1, random field, t=12000): division survives the isotropic drift (11 and 10 persistent splits, generation 2 and 3, 0 merges) and the dumbbells point in several directions; Supported
summary: I ran the finding's world_iso.py with WORLD_P {"ISO":1} (spectral enzyme-drift flux; the file's default is ISO=0), labkit 120 frames, t=12000, on seeds 3 and 4 from the default random field. Both runs nucleate 3-6 bodies by t~500 that elongate into dumbbells and pinch into round daughters: persistent splits 11 and 10, max generation 2 and 3, 0 merges, 17 bodies at the end on both seeds (c39's seed 1: 9, generation 2, 0 merges). On seed 4 (rerun/seed4/sheet.png) dumbbells lie on both diagonals (t=2100-2600: one along each) and near the horizontal (t=8400-11000), so no single locked axis; this matches the finding's claim that the grid set the axis, not the division. I did not re-run the ISO=0 arm.

observations.D: rerun/seed3/FACTS.md: 11 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 merges; rerun/seed4/FACTS.md: 10, generation 3, 0 merges; rerun/seed4/sheet.png dumbbells on both diagonals and the horizontal

seeds_run.result: pass: 10 persistent splits, generation 3, 0 merges, several division axes

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds of the ISO=1 arm only; I did not re-run ISO=0 on these seeds, so the axis comparison rests on the finding's runs and my reading of the sheets (no orientation statistic). The spectral flux is not monotone and its effect on e bounds was not checked.
